A1.justification: Both 17-page PDFs describe the same DCAE study and include the main text, references, and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable assessment; pages 3–17 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression-performance, latency, ablation, and visualization results in Section 4 and Appendices B–E, including entropy-model substitution experiments in Table 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and the supplementary entropy-model substitution experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dictionary-based cross-attention model, multi-scale feature aggregation, latent residual prediction, encoder-decoder architecture, and training objective. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenImages for training and Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC Professional Validation for evaluation. The appendices retain the same tasks, images, and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, the global-token comparison in Table 5, the ELIC/TCM/FTIC experiments in Table 6, and the expanded benchmark comparisons in Appendix E.

E3.justification: Training budgets, crop and batch sizes, model configurations, ablation settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both versions retain the same PSNR, MS-SSIM, BD-rate, latency, and computational-cost evaluations.

E4.justification: The DCA/MSFA component ablations, dictionary-size and convolution-depth studies, global-token comparison, and supplementary entropy-model substitutions are identical. Attention visualizations and reconstruction case studies are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised in the main text or appendices.

E6.justification: All reported results remain unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 193 ms total latency and BD-rates of -17.0%, -21.1%, and -19.7% on Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC, respectively. Supplementary numerical results, curves, and qualitative examples also match.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same mathematical formulation and Equations 1–8, including the rate-distortion objective and dictionary-attention definitions. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The dictionary-prior, multi-scale querying, and state-of-the-art performance claims remain in the abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion. v2 removes one redundant introductory sentence about outperforming existing methods without changing the retained claims' meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of dictionary sharing, attention-map behavior, saturation with larger dictionaries or deeper MSFA, and advantages over transmitted global tokens are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain identical implementation, architecture, hyperparameter, and hardware information. The printed code-repository link is also unchanged; the corresponding-author note adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 52 reference entries are unchanged. The positioning of learned dictionary priors relative to internal-dependency models and earlier dictionary approaches is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author marker and note for Shuhang Gu, shortens wording in the introduction, and replaces a redundant performance sentence with a transition to the contributions. Section order and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added author footnote and introduction edits cause localized text reflow on pages 1–2, alongside the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Figures 1–16 and Tables 1–6 retain their content and presentation; pages 3–17 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 makes small introductory edits and clarifies corresponding-author attribution, while retaining the entire method, experimental evidence, technical documentation, and appendices. These administrative and editorial changes do not materially improve or weaken the paper's clarity, rigor, or scientific support.
